newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Nemtsov to head natural resources body.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Nemtsov to head natural resources body.

text.p: Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov, a reformist in charge of the energy sector, will head a special government commission overseeing production-sharing deals, Interfax news agency said on Tuesday.
The commission, now being set up, could give foreign energy and mineral investors a channel through which to lobby to get their often-stalled projects off the ground.
Interfax said Nemtsov, who is also fuel and energy minister, would be joined by First Deputy Fuel and Energy Minister Sergei Kiriyenko and Natural Resources Minister Viktor Orlov.
Russia has a production-sharing law and several multi-billion dollar energy contracts with Western, Japanese and other oil investors.
But Moscow is only slowly deciding which hydrocarbon and mineral reserves it will offer for development on a production-sharing basis and there are conflicts with other legislation.
It was not known whether Nemtsov's commission would encourage parliament to approve quickly reserves open to output-sharing deals.
Foreign energy companies plan about $60-$70 billion in direct investment in Russia once the proper legislation is in place.
